records.reason: m53 at PE/EA 50/1 probes a conjugated aliphatic aldehyde in a weak mobile phase. Its broad predictor quantile ranges and high CW distance make it useful for testing transfer from aromatic to aliphatic carbonyl response.

m199 is diphenyl sulfoxide. Its 1/1, 100 uL condition supplies a lower-ratio loading reference for a molecule with a steep measured retention response, helping distinguish baseline loading behavior from the late regime.

m34 in pure EA at 150 uL provides a strong-mobile-phase fluoroacetophenone reference. It constrains endpoint behavior before transferring corrections to the weaker PE-rich conditions represented elsewhere in the batch.

m78 at 10/1 and 150 uL probes a benzyl-substituted beta-ketoester. It tests whether carbonyl spacing and substitution predict the intermediate retention response without treating all multifunctional esters alike.

m4 at 20/1 samples a brominated fused hydrocarbon predicted to start early but finish substantially later. This tests whether aromatic surface and fusion can alter V2 independently of polar functional groups.

m145 at 10/1 supplies an ortho-methylbenzaldehyde point. Its label can teach how local substitution around an aldehyde affects onset and finish relative to aromatic ketones and less crowded aldehydes.

m154 at 10/1 and 150 uL probes an iodinated trifluoromethoxy aromatic. Together with its selected 5/1 condition and existing measurements, it tests ether and halogen response while acknowledging the loading difference.
m103 at 1/1, 100 uL pairs with its selected 5/1 row at identical sample amount and DCM loading volume. This isolates solvent-ratio response in methyl iodobenzoate.

m56 at 100/1 and 50 uL extends the weak-mobile-phase end of an aromatic ester response curve. It tests whether V2 grows while onset remains comparatively early, using existing higher-load measurements as references.

m97 at 20/1 and 100 uL probes a bromophenylacetate approaching its late regime. Alongside the selected 10/1 condition and existing measurements, it helps resolve solvent response and loading dependence.
m15 at 20/1 and 100 uL supplies a simple cyclohexyl acrylate control. Its label helps prevent multifunctional-carbonyl corrections from spreading to ordinary single-esters in the PE-rich regime.

m177 at 20/1 and 150 uL tests the model's compact prediction for nitrobenzophenone. The result can distinguish a real structural exception from inappropriate transfer of late behavior from other nitro-carbonyl graphs.

m1 at 5/1 and 50 uL supplies a simple bromopropylbenzene reference. It constrains ordinary hydrophobic onset and finish across loading conditions, limiting unintended changes from polar-family retraining.
m85 at 5/1 and 100 uL probes ethyl fluorobenzoate between existing conditions. It provides a single-ester contrast to methoxybenzoate and multifunctional beta-ketoester responses.

m48 in pure EA at 50 uL samples a small nonaromatic hypochlorite graph. This extends compact-condition calibration beyond the dominant aromatic scaffolds without assuming its oxygen behaves like a carbonyl acceptor.
m103 at 5/1 matches the selected 1/1 row in sample amount, loading solvent, and loading-solvent volume. The pair directly measures how solvent ratio changes V1 and V2 in a halogenated aromatic ester.
m2 at 20/1 pairs with its selected 50/1 condition at fixed 100 uL sample and 300 uL DCM loading. This tests ratio sensitivity in a donor-free dibromomethyl aromatic.
m180 at 1/1 probes tetralone under a relatively strong mobile phase. It anchors the compact side of a fused cyclic ketone response and supports transfer to larger fused aromatic carbonyls.
m36 at 1/1 and 150 uL tests aminoacetophenone at higher sample loading. It helps identify whether donor/basic functionality changes V1 and V2 differently from neutral aromatic ketones.
m2 at 50/1 completes a fixed-loading ratio contrast with its selected 20/1 row. The model predicts a small onset reversal and nearly unchanged finish; measurement can test this nonmonotonic response.
m157 at 50/1 and 150 uL supplies a high-load diiodobenzene control in a weak mobile phase. It constrains heavy-halogen behavior independently of carbonyl, donor, or basic-ring interactions.
m40 at 5/1 and 150 uL fills an intermediate acetylnaphthalene condition. This helps interpolate between its compact strong-mobile-phase behavior and much later PE-rich measurements.

m89 at 1/1 and 100 uL probes ethyl anthranilate at an intermediate loading. It tests whether the ortho amino-ester environment remains compact before the molecule's stronger retention at higher PE/EA ratios.

m97 at 10/1 and 150 uL complements the selected 20/1 row. Existing loading references make this useful for learning whether the bromophenylacetate transition depends mainly on ratio or also on amount.

m42 at 10/1 and 100 uL fills a simple acetophenone condition between measured lower and higher ratios. It calibrates onset growth in a common carbonyl scaffold without imposing the response of multifunctional analogues.
m193 in pure EA at 100 uL anchors nitrobenzaldehyde before its pronounced PE-rich retention. It helps teach solvent sensitivity separately from a global nitro or carbonyl polarity correction.

m87 at 10/1 and 50 uL tests the condition preceding its measured 20/1 response. Its relatively broad quantile ranges warrant checking response curvature after the recent overprediction at the higher ratio.
m105 at 5/1 and 100 uL probes methyl salicylate. Its ortho donor-ester arrangement provides a structural control for deciding when donor-containing oxygenated graphs develop broad finishes.
m210 at 2/1 and 150 uL supplies a biphenyl loading point. It constrains donor-free aromatic endpoint width and guards against transferring polar-family tail corrections to hydrophobic rows.

m80 at 5/1 and 100 uL tests diethyl malonate at the loading used for its previously overpredicted PE-rich conditions. This compact control can teach why multiple ester acceptors do not universally imply late retention.

m156 in pure EA at 50 uL has a surprisingly broad predicted finish for pentafluorobenzene. Measuring it tests an unusual neutral condition response instead of assuming all hydrophobic rows are routine.
m154 at 5/1 and 50 uL complements its selected 10/1 row and existing loading references. It tests whether halogenated aromatic ether endpoints respond smoothly to ratio and amount.

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl and oxygenated retention responses depend strongly on functional-group arrangement and solvent ratio; acceptor count or donor presence alone cannot predict whether V1 shifts, V2 broadens, or both occur.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Endpoint-specific labels from related carbonyl and ester graphs can repair large tail failures while preserving compact oxygenated predictions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which local structural features determine the solvent-ratio range in which onset moves later versus finish broadens?

hypotheses.content: Hydrophobic aromatic rows include condition-specific onset and finish anomalies, making a universal compact-neutral response unsafe even though many neutral controls are routine.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local neutral condition contrasts can distinguish transferable ratio effects from isolated anomalies and constrain unwanted changes caused by polar-family corrections.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do unusual neutral predictions persist across nearby ratios and loading amounts, or are they confined to individual condition tuples?

feedback_interpretation: The latest measured batch revealed a large V2 underestimate for the dimethoxy aldehyde, while the methoxy aromatic ester and fluorinated cyclopropyl ketone had much smaller discrepancies. Many neutral controls were close, and several rows showed different error directions for V1 and V2. This favors endpoint-specific condition curves and structural controls over blanket tail corrections. Historical acquisition errors guide these choices; they are not current-model residuals. Predictor quantile ranges provide supporting signals rather than calibrated epistemic uncertainty.
batch_rationale: The batch preserves 32 distinct eligible candidate rows. The m2 and m103 pairs hold loading fixed while changing PE/EA, directly testing solvent response. The m97 and m154 selections add condition and loading contrasts interpreted alongside existing measurements. Carbonyl, ester, sulfoxide, amino, and phenolic environments test transfer between compact and late regimes, while hydrophobic and halogenated controls constrain ordinary Row behavior and unusual neutral predictions. Higher PE/EA ratios correspond to weaker mobile phases on normal-phase silica; pure EA supplies the stronger-solvent anchors. These labels can improve generalization by teaching separate onset and finish responses without assuming monotonicity, universal tails, or unrecorded experimental variables.
